title: Hepatocellular Carcinomas with Concomitant Mutations of TERT, TP53, and CTNNB1: Is There a Role for Artificial Intelligence?
authors: Chillotti, Stefano; Maloberti, Thais; Degiovanni, Alessio; Malvi, Deborah; D'Errico, Antonia; de Biase, Dario; Vasuri, Francesco
one_liner_zh: 该文报道肝癌中TERT/TP53/CTNNB1共突变病例，仅提及AI未来可能用于形态-遗传分类，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: TP53, CTNNB1, and TERT-promoter mutations are the most common driver mutations in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The morphological and genetical HCC heterogeneities are difficult to discriminate by the eye of the pathologist. Here, we describe two rare cases of HCC with simultaneous co-mutation of all three of genes, which represent a poorly described occurrence in the literature. In these two cases, areas with different tumor grade and different beta-catenin and Glutamine Synthetase expression (performed by automated immunohistochemistry) were observed. NGS analysis was performed in these different areas, to check for potential diversity of mutation burden on the different regions, but no differences were found: all micro-areas analyzed showed the co-presence of mutations in TP53, CTNNB1, and TERT. The evidence that all mutations were found in all the different areas analyzed by NGS leads to hypothesize that the tumor is not composed of different clones harboring different mutations. All the variants are harbored by the same neoplastic clone, albeit leading to different phenotypes. Mutation prediction Artificial Intelligence models could help the morpho-genetic classification of HCC in the future, since they can find variabilities not obvious to the human eye, with increased sensitivity, specificity and reproducibility.
abstract_zh: TP53、CTNNB1和TERT启动子突变是肝细胞癌（HCC）中最常见的驱动突变。肝细胞癌的形态学和遗传学异质性难以通过病理学家的肉眼进行区分。在此，我们描述了两例罕见的HCC病例，其同时存在这三个基因的共突变，这在文献中属于描述较少的现象。在这两例病例中，观察到不同肿瘤分级以及不同β-catenin和谷氨酰胺合成酶表达（通过自动免疫组织化学检测）的区域。对这些不同区域进行了NGS分析，以检查不同区域突变负荷的潜在差异，但未发现差异：所有分析的微小区域均显示TP53、CTNNB1和TERT突变的共存。所有突变在NGS分析的所有不同区域中均被发现，这一证据提示肿瘤并非由携带不同突变的多个克隆组成。所有变异均由同一肿瘤克隆携带，尽管导致了不同的表型。突变预测人工智能模型未来可能有助于HCC的形态-遗传学分类，因为它们能够发现人眼不易察觉的变异性，具有更高的敏感性、特异性和可重复性。
